tagline: From an old meetinghouse in Abington north to Pomfret Center.
intro: Route 97 comes a long way up from Norwich, but the scenic part is the last four and a half miles, from its southern junction with US 44 at Abington to its end at US 44 and Route 169 in Pomfret Center.

This stretch was a state highway of its own in 1922, the road from Abington to Pomfret Center, and was folded into Route 97 in 1934. Pomfret takes its name from Pontefract in West Yorkshire and has no formal town center, only several villages, Abington and Pomfret Center among them.

moments.title: Abington Congregational Church
moments.text: Just south of the scenic start, on the east side of Route 97, stands the meetinghouse of 1751, the oldest church building in Connecticut in continuous religious use.

moments.title: Pomfret Center
moments.text: Near the end of the run the old Boston Turnpike, Route 244, comes in from the west, and Route 97 carries its line the rest of the way to US 44.
